title: Most writes notify nobody
body: Webhook dispatch is wired at the router, not at the event store. Only commands/router.py and views/router.py call it, so a webhook subscriber sees objects created through the public API but misses every edit made in the workspace, every Obsidian or Notion import, every WebDAV save and every federated patch.
ev: rg 'webhook_service.dispatch' → commands/router.py ×2, views/router.py ×1, main.py ×1 (registration). 28 event_store.commit() sites in total.

title: Imported data is never SHACL-checked
body: Validation is enqueued by the caller rather than by the store. browser, commands, views, task_templates and inference enqueue; obsidian, notion, rdf_import, vfs and federation do not. A vault import can land thousands of objects that the lint panel will never mention until something else touches them.
ev: rg '.enqueue(' by module → browser 3, commands 2, views 1, task_templates 1, inference 1. No hits in obsidian/, notion/, rdf_import/, vfs/, federation/.

title: The single-write-door convention is aspirational
body: CLAUDE.md and CODEBASE.md both state that all mutations go through POST /api/commands. In practice 26 of the 28 event_store.commit() call sites are outside the commands module, and six modules import the command handlers directly to build Operations themselves. The invariant that does hold is the deeper one — nothing writes raw SPARQL UPDATE, everything goes through the event store.
ev: event_store.commit by module → browser 8, notion 4, obsidian 3, vfs 2, rdf_import 2, inference 2, federation 2, commands 2, views 1, task_templates 1, services 1.

title: The documentation is five months behind the code
body: CODEBASE.md is dated 12 March and describes 24 modules, 2 mental models and 82 specs in 28 directories. The tree holds 39 modules, 8 models and 126 specs in 55 directories. Federation, apps, copilot, context, ontology, notion, dashboard and persona do not appear in it at all, and it still describes browser/router.py as a 1,570-line monolith — that file is now a 38-line aggregator.
ev: CODEBASE.md header 'Last updated: 2026-03-12'; ls backend/app → 39 dirs; ls models → 8; find e2e/tests -name '*.spec.ts' → 126; wc -l backend/app/browser/router.py → 38.

title: Presentation modules hold the most write sites
body: In a volatility-based reading, browser/ and vfs/ are client-tier: they render pages and serve files. Between them they hold 10 of the 28 commit sites, reaching past the managers tier straight into resource access. Nothing is broken by it, but the write surface is now spread across the layer that changes most often.
ev: browser/{objects,comments,events}.py → 8 commit sites; vfs/write.py → 2. Both import from app.commands.handlers directly.

title: A dependency provider exists and is skipped
body: dependencies.py exposes get_event_store(), which hands out the singleton built during lifespan startup. Three routers construct EventStore(client) inline instead. It is harmless while the store is stateless — and precisely the kind of thing that stops being harmless the day it is not.

title: Two files carry outsized responsibility
body: views/service.py is 3,859 lines — the largest file in the backend — inside a module of only four files totalling 5,923 lines. ontology/service.py is 2,277. Both are candidates for the split that browser/ already received, which turned a 1,570-line router into 17 focused files.

title: 330 broad exception handlers
body: except Exception or bare except appears 330 times across the backend package. Some are deliberate — webhook dispatch and scheduler ticks should swallow failures — but at that volume the deliberate ones are indistinguishable from the defensive ones.

title: Named graphs grow without bound
body: One immutable named graph per write, kept forever. That is the intended trade for a complete audit trail rather than a leak, but nothing in the tree prunes, compacts or archives them, so store size tracks total write count for the life of the instance.
ev: events/store.py mints urn:sempkm:event:{uuid} per commit; no deletion path in the module.

title: The validation queue is in-process
body: An asyncio queue held in memory and started in the lifespan. A container restart drops whatever was pending; validation is re-triggered by the next write rather than resumed.
ev: validation/queue.py — AsyncValidationQueue, started in main.py lifespan, no persistence.

title: Every previously recorded concern is fixed
body: The February planning notes listed SMTP delivery as a stub, the session cookie as hardcoded insecure, the label cache as never invalidated and Alembic as wired up but unused. All four are resolved in the current tree — and the notes were never updated to say so.
ev: services/email.py uses aiosmtplib; auth/router.py:54 reads settings.cookie_secure; label invalidate() called from 6 sites; 26 files in backend/migrations/versions/.

title: No TODO, FIXME or HACK markers anywhere in the backend
body: Zero occurrences across 169,932 lines of Python. Unusual at this size, and it means the findings above had to come from reading structure rather than from the trail of notes a codebase usually leaves about itself.
